passages.note: Bill Status page names Kolodin as prime sponsor of HB2785, an act whose own short title spans primary dates, identification, canvass, recounts and ballots.
House Third Reading shows Kolodin voting Yea on HB2785, a multi-subject elections-administration bill, so the vote alone cannot pick out the identification clause.

passages.provision_quote: ANY VOTING LOCATION THE VOTER MAY CHOOSE TO PROVIDE IDENTIFICATION WHEN PRESENTING THE VOTER'S MAILED EARLY BALLOT, AND IF SO THE ELECTION OFFICIAL SHALL: ( a ) REQUIRE THE VOTER TO PRESENT IDENTIFICATION THAT COMPLIES WITH PARAGRAPH 1 OF THIS SUBSECTION.
passages.note: The bill's only identification change lets a voter optionally show ID with a mailed early ballot; it does not require ID on every mail ballot, remove ID at the polls, or touch registration proof of citizenship.

rows.reasoning: HB2785 (2024), a bill Kolodin prime-sponsored and voted Yea on (56-2-0-0-2), is titled 'primary; identification; canvass; recounts; ballots' and its content covers those several unrelated administrative subjects, so it is multi-subject. Its one identification-related change lets a voter optionally present ID with a mailed early ballot at a voting location rather than requiring photo ID in person and an ID number on every mail ballot, so even isolated it does not match a rung's clause. Without Kolodin's own words tying his sponsorship or vote to that specific provision, no rung is established.
